A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our results support the hypothesis that error processing is mediated by a mechanism that assigns negative value to states of the system that produce incorrect responses.

we have developed a model that is able to simulate behavioral and brain potential data from a speeded response task and that is able to do so without requiring a separate mechanism for error monitoring and detection.

The main takeaway from our work is that

a simple mechanism for error detection, based on the assignment of value to states of the system, provides a parsimonious account of a wide range of empirical data from speeded response time experiments.
a mechanism for error detection can be formalized and implemented in a computational model that can account for a variety of behavioral and electrophysiological data in a speed of response task.
